facts.statement: The genus Velociraptor was formally described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1924.
facts.quote: authority: Osborn, 1924

facts.statement: Velociraptor lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch, approximately 75 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Velociraptor (; ) is a genus of small dromaeosaurid dinosaurs that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous epoch, about 75 million to 71 million years ago (Mya).

facts.statement: Velociraptor was a small dinosaur measuring between 1.5 and 2.07 meters in length and weighing between 14.1 and 19.7 kilograms.
facts.quote: Smaller than other dromaeosaurids like Deinonychus and Achillobator, Velociraptor was about 1.5 - 2.07 m long with a body mass of around 14.1 - 19.7 kg.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was a bipedal, feathered carnivore featuring a long tail and enlarged sickle-shaped claws on its hind feet used for tackling prey.
facts.quote: It was a bipedal, feathered carnivore with a long tail and an enlarged sickle-shaped claw on each hindfoot, which is thought to have been used to tackle and restrain prey.

facts.statement: Velociraptor is distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long, low skull and upturned snout.
facts.quote: Velociraptor can be distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long and low skull, with an upturned snout.

facts.statement: The first known Velociraptor fossil, a crushed complete skull with a manual claw, was discovered by Peter Kaisen on August 11, 1923, in the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: During an American Museum of Natural History expedition to the Flaming Cliffs (Bayn Dzak or Bayanzag) of the Djadochta Formation, Gobi Desert, on 11 August 1923, Peter Kaisen discovered the first Velociraptor fossil known to science—a crushed but complete skull, associated with one manual claw and adjoining phalanges (AMNH 6515).

facts.statement: The famous "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen was discovered by a Polish-Mongolian team in 1971.
facts.quote: The most famous is part of the "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen (MPC-D 100/25; formerly IGM, GIN, or GI SPS), discovered by a Polish-Mongolian team in 1971.

facts.statement: A complete juvenile skeleton including a skull was reported by Rinchen Barsbold and Halszka Osmólska in 1999.
facts.quote: In 1999, Rinchen Barsbold and Halszka Osmólska reported a juvenile Velociraptor specimen (GIN or IGM 100/2000), represented by a complete skeleton including the skull of a young individual.

facts.statement: The species Velociraptor osmolskae was named by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in 2008.
facts.quote: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named these bones V. osmolskae (for Polish paleontologist Halszka Osmólska) in 2008.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Velociraptor osmolskae belongs to the genus Velociraptor, as a 2013 study suggested it is closer to Linheraptor and may make the genus paraphyletic.
facts.quote: However, the 2013 study noted that while "the elongate shape of the maxilla in V. osmolskae is similar to that of V. mongoliensis," phylogenetic analysis found it to be closer to Linheraptor, making the genus paraphyletic; thus, V. osmolskae might not actually belong to the genus Velociraptor and requires reassessment.

facts.statement: Mark J. Powers concluded in 2020 that specimen MPC-D 100/982 represents a new and third species of Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Mark J. Powers in his 2020 master thesis fully described MPC-D 100/982, which he concluded to represent a new and third species of Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Some estimates suggest Velociraptor could have reached lengths of about 2.5 meters and weighed up to 28 kilograms.
facts.quote: Some estimates suggest that Velociraptor may have been larger, possibly reaching lengths of about 2.5 m (8 ft) and weighing up to 28 kg (60 lb).

facts.statement: Quill knobs indicating a feather covering have been reported on the ulna of a Velociraptor specimen estimated to be 1.5 meters long and 15 kilograms in weight.
facts.quote: Prominent quill knobs—attachment site of "wing" feathers and direct indicator of a feather covering—have been reported from the ulna of a single Velociraptor specimen (IGM 100/981), which represents an animal of estimated 1.5 m long and 15 kg in weight.

facts.statement: Velociraptor is classified as a genus of small dromaeosaurid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Velociraptor (; ) is a genus of small dromaeosaurid dinosaurs

facts.statement: The skull of Velociraptor was elongated and could reach a length of 23 centimeters.
facts.quote: The skull of Velociraptor was rather elongated and grew up to 23 cm long.

facts.statement: The snout made up about 60% of the skull length and was narrow, formed primarily by the nasal, premaxilla, and maxilla bones.
facts.quote: The snout, which occupied about 60% of the entire skull length, was notably narrow and mainly formed by the nasal, premaxilla, and maxilla bones.

facts.statement: The premaxilla was the frontmost bone of the skull and was longer than it was tall.
facts.quote: The premaxilla was the anteriormost bone in the skull, and it was longer than taller.

facts.statement: The maxilla was nearly triangular and was the largest bone element of the snout.
facts.quote: The maxilla was nearly triangular in shape and the largest element of the snout.

facts.statement: Both the premaxilla and maxilla possessed multiple tooth sockets on their lower surfaces.
facts.quote: Both premaxilla and maxilla had several alveoli (tooth sockets) on their bottom surfaces.

facts.statement: The premaxilla held four teeth while the maxilla held eleven teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla had 4 alveoli (meaning that 4 teeth were developed), and the maxilla had 11 alveoli.

facts.statement: The lower jaw dentary contained between 14 and 15 tooth sockets.
facts.quote: At the dentary, between 14–15 alveoli were present.

facts.statement: Velociraptor's teeth were mostly uniform in shape but featured serrations that were sharper on the back edge than the front.
facts.quote: The teeth of Velociraptor were fairly homodont (equal in shape) and had several denticles (serrations), each more strongly serrated on the back edge than the front.

facts.statement: Velociraptor had a large hand with three long fingers ending in curved claws that were structurally similar to modern bird wing bones.
facts.quote: Velociraptor, like other dromaeosaurids, had a large manus with three elongated digits (fingers), which ended up in strongly curved unguals (claw bones) that were similar in construction and flexibility to the wing bones of modern birds.

facts.statement: The middle finger was the longest digit, while the first finger was the shortest.
facts.quote: The second digit was the longest of the three digits present, while the first was shortest.

facts.statement: Velociraptor's wrist bones prevented the hand from turning downward, forcing it to be held with the palm facing inward.
facts.quote: The structure of the carpal (wrist) bones prevented pronation of the wrist and forced the manus to be held with the palmar surface facing inward (medially), not downward.

facts.statement: Velociraptor walked on its third and fourth toes because its famous second toe was held retracted off the ground.
facts.quote: The second digit, for which Velociraptor is most famous, was highly modified and held retracted off the ground, which caused Velociraptor and other dromaeosaurids to walk on only their third and fourth digits.

facts.statement: The enlarged sickle claw on the second toe could grow to over 6.5 centimeters in length and was likely used to restrain prey.
facts.quote: This enlarged claw, which could grow to over 6.5 cm long around its outer edge, was most likely a predatory device used to restrain struggling prey.

facts.statement: While it was once believed that Velociraptor's tail was stiff and rod-like, fossil evidence of an S-shaped tail suggests it had significant horizontal flexibility.
facts.quote: These were once thought to fully stiffen the tail, forcing the entire tail to act as a single rod-like unit. However, at least one specimen has preserved a series of intact tail vertebrae curved sideways into an S-shape, suggesting that there was considerably more horizontal flexibility than once thought.

facts.statement: Velociraptor belongs to the group Eudromaeosauria, which is a subgroup of the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Velociraptor is a member of the group Eudromaeosauria, a derived sub-group of the larger family Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: Velociraptor is frequently classified within its own subfamily known as Velociraptorinae.
facts.quote: It is often placed within its own subfamily, Velociraptorinae.

facts.statement: Some 2010s studies suggest that Velociraptorinae is not a distinct group but a paraphyletic grade that gave rise to Dromaeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Several studies published during the 2010s, including expanded versions of the analyses that found support for Velociraptorinae, have failed to resolve it as a distinct group, but rather have suggested it is a paraphyletic grade which gave rise to the Dromaeosaurinae.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was first described in 1924 and was initially classified in the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: When first described in 1924, Velociraptor was placed in the family Megalosauridae, as was the case with most carnivorous dinosaurs at the time

facts.statement: Some authors have classified all dromaeosaurids, including Velociraptor, in the family Archaeopterygidae, effectively making them flightless birds.
facts.quote: All dromaeosaurids have also been referred to the family Archaeopterygidae by at least one author (which would, in effect, make Velociraptor a flightless bird).

facts.statement: Several studies suggest that V. osmolskae is distantly related to V. mongoliensis.
facts.quote: However, several studies have found "V." osmolskae to be distantly related to V. mongoliensis.

facts.statement: In 2007, researchers found six quill knobs on the ulna of a Velociraptor fossil from the Djadochta Formation, indicating the presence of feathers.
facts.quote: In 2007 Alan H. Turner and colleagues reported the presence of six quill knobs in the ulna of a referred Velociraptor specimen (IGM 100/981) from the Ukhaa Tolgod locality of the Djadochta Formation.

facts.statement: The presence of feathers on Velociraptor suggests that larger flightless maniraptorans did not lose feathers secondarily because of their size.
facts.quote: Turner and colleagues interpreted the presence of feathers on Velociraptor as evidence against the idea that the larger, flightless maniraptorans lost their feathers secondarily due to larger body size.

facts.statement: Velociraptor feathers may have been used for display, nest brooding, or to aid in running up slopes.
facts.quote: The feathers of the flightless Velociraptor may have been used for display, for covering their nests while brooding, or for added speed and thrust when running up inclined slopes.

facts.statement: Velociraptor could hear sound frequencies between 2,368 and 3,965 Hz, aiding in prey tracking.
facts.quote: Examinations of the endocranium of Velociraptor indicate that it was able to detect and hear a wide range of sound frequencies (2,368–3,965 Hz) and could track prey with ease as a result.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was an opportunistic predator that sometimes scavenged carrion during droughts, famine, or when in poor health.
facts.quote: Fossil evidence suggesting Velociraptor scavenged also indicates that it was an opportunistic and actively predatory animal, feeding on carrion during times of drought or famine, if in poor health, or depending on the animal's age.

facts.statement: Velociraptor had a bite force of 304 N, which is lower than that of Dromaeosaurus (885 N) and Deinonychus (706 N).
facts.quote: Among studied taxa, Velociraptor was scored with a bite force of 304 N, which was lower than that of other dromaeosaurids such as Dromaeosaurus (885 N) or Deinonychus (706 N).

facts.statement: A 1971 fossil specimen shows a Velociraptor and a Protoceratops locked in combat, providing direct evidence of their predatory behavior.
facts.quote: The "Fighting Dinosaurs" specimen, found in 1971, preserves a Velociraptor mongoliensis and Protoceratops andrewsi in combat and provides direct evidence of predatory behavior.

facts.statement: The "Fighting Dinosaurs" fossil is now thought to result from rapid burial by sand from a collapsing dune or sandstorm, rather than drowning.
facts.quote: When originally reported, it was hypothesized that the two animals drowned. However, as the animals were preserved in ancient sand dune deposits, it is now thought that the animals were buried in sand, either from a collapsing dune or in a sandstorm.

facts.statement: Scleral ring comparisons suggest Velociraptor was likely nocturnal, implying the "Fighting Dinosaurs" encounter occurred at twilight or in low light.
facts.quote: Comparisons between the scleral rings of Velociraptor, Protoceratops, and modern birds and reptiles indicates that Velociraptor may have been nocturnal, while Protoceratops may have been cathemeral, active throughout the day during short intervals, suggesting that the fight may have occurred at twilight or during low-light conditions.

facts.statement: The "Fighting Dinosaurs" fossil suggests Velociraptor used its sickle claw to pierce vital throat organs rather than slash the abdomen.
facts.quote: This suggests Velociraptor may have used its sickle claw to pierce vital organs of the throat, such as the jugular vein, carotid artery, or trachea (windpipe), rather than slashing the abdomen.

facts.statement: The preserved bony core of Velociraptor's sickle claw has a rounded inner edge, suggesting it was not designed for slashing.
facts.quote: The inside edge of the claw was rounded and not unusually sharp, which may have precluded any sort of cutting or slashing action, although only the bony core of the claw is preserved.

facts.statement: A 2005 BBC experiment showed that a replica Velociraptor claw could penetrate but not tear open a pork belly, challenging the slashing hypothesis.
facts.quote: The slashing hypothesis was tested during a 2005 BBC documentary, The Truth About Killer Dinosaurs. The producers of the program created an artificial Velociraptor leg with a sickle claw and used a pork belly to simulate the dinosaur's prey. Though the sickle claw did penetrate the abdominal wall, it was unable to tear it open, indicating that the claw was not used to disembowel prey.

facts.statement: Despite popular depictions, there is no specific fossil evidence that Velociraptor hunted in packs.
facts.quote: Although many isolated fossils of Velociraptor have been found in Mongolia, none were closely associated with other individuals. Therefore, while Velociraptor is commonly depicted as a pack hunter, as in Jurassic Park, there is only limited fossil evidence to support this theory for dromaeosaurids in general and none specific to Velociraptor itself.

facts.statement: In 2011, researchers proposed the "raptor prey restraint" model, suggesting Velociraptor killed prey by pinning it with its body weight and sickle claws, similar to eagles.
facts.quote: In 2011, Denver Fowler and colleagues suggested a new method by which dromaeosaurs like Velociraptor and similar dromaeosaurs may have captured and restrained prey. This model, known as the "raptor prey restraint" (RPR) model of predation, proposes that dromaeosaurs killed their prey in a manner very similar to extant accipitrid birds of prey: by leaping onto their quarry, pinning it under their body weight, and gripping it tightly with the large, sickle-shaped claws.

facts.statement: Velociraptor's feathered arms may have acted as stabilizers for balance while pinning prey, aided by a stiff tail.
facts.quote: The arms, which could exert a lot of force but were likely covered in long feathers, may have been used as flapping stabilizers for balance while atop a struggling prey animal, along with the stiff counterbalancing tail.

facts.statement: Velociraptor's weak jaws may have been used for sawing bites to finish off prey pinned by its claws, similar to a Komodo dragon.
facts.quote: The jaws, thought by Fowler and colleagues to be comparatively weak, would have been useful for row saw motion bites like the modern day Komodo dragon, which also has a weak bite, to finish off its prey if the kicks were not powerful enough.

facts.statement: In 2010, researchers published findings from a 2008 discovery of Velociraptor teeth found near a Protoceratops jaw with bite marks in the Bayan Mandahu Formation.
facts.quote: In 2010, Hone and colleagues published a paper on their 2008 discovery of shed teeth of what they believed to be a Velociraptor near a tooth-marked jaw bone of what they believed to be a Protoceratops in the Bayan Mandahu Formation.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that a specific fossil find represented late-stage scavenging of a Protoceratops carcass by a Velociraptor.
facts.quote: The authors concluded that the find represented "late-stage carcass consumption by Velociraptor" as the predator would have eaten other parts of a freshly killed Protoceratops before biting in the jaw area.

facts.statement: Researchers theorize that Velociraptor's high bite force resistance was an adaptation for scavenging rather than active predation.
facts.quote: It is theorized by the authors that high bite force resistance was an adaptation towards obtaining food through scavenging more often than through active predation in Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was warm-blooded to some degree due to the high energy requirements of hunting.
facts.quote: Velociraptor was warm-blooded to some degree, as it required a significant amount of energy to hunt.

facts.statement: Bone growth rates suggest Velociraptor had a more moderate metabolism than most modern warm-blooded mammals and birds.
facts.quote: However, bone growth rates in dromaeosaurids and some early birds suggest a more moderate metabolism, compared with most modern warm-blooded mammals and birds.

facts.statement: Analysis of nasal cavity size suggests Velociraptor had less developed nasal thermoregulation than modern warm-blooded animals.
facts.quote: They found that the size of the nasal cavity relative to the head size of extant endotherms is larger than those of extant ectotherms, and among taxa, Velociraptor was recovered below the extant endotherms level by reconstructing its nasal respiratory cavity.

facts.statement: In 1995, researchers reported a Velociraptor skull with puncture wounds matching the spacing and size of Velociraptor teeth, suggesting an intraspecific fight.
facts.quote: Norell with colleagues in 1995 reported one V. mongoliensis skull bearing two parallel rows of small punctures on its frontal bones that, upon closer examination, match the spacing and size of Velociraptor teeth.

facts.statement: The lack of healing around bite wounds on a specific Velociraptor skull suggests it was killed by another Velociraptor.
facts.quote: Because its bone structure shows no sign of healing near the bite wounds and the overall specimen was not scavenged, this individual was likely killed by this fatal wound.

facts.statement: In 2012, researchers reported a sub-adult Velociraptor specimen with a broken rib and pterosaur bones in its stomach, indicating it died shortly after sustaining the injury.
facts.quote: In 2012 David Hone and team reported another injured Velociraptor specimen (MPC-D 100/54, roughly a sub-adult individual) found with the bones of an azhdarchid pterosaur within its stomach cavity, was carrying or recovering from an injury sustained to one broken rib.

facts.statement: Velociraptor osmolskae lived alongside various species including Pinacosaurus, Linhenykus, Linheraptor, Machairasaurus, Bagaceratops, and others in the Bayan Mandahu Formation.
facts.quote: V. osmolskae lived alongside the ankylosaurid Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus; alvarezsaurid Linhenykus; closely related dromaeosaurid Linheraptor; oviraptorids Machairasaurus and Wulatelong; protoceratopsids Bagaceratops and Protoceratops hellenikorhinus; and troodontids Linhevenator, Papiliovenator, and Philovenator.

facts.statement: Specimens of Velociraptor mongoliensis have been recovered from the Djadochta Formation in the Mongolian province of Ömnögovi.
facts.quote: Known specimens of Velociraptor mongoliensis have been recovered from the Djadochta Formation (also spelled Djadokhta), in the Mongolian province of Ömnögovi.

facts.statement: The Djadochta Formation dates to the Campanian stage, between 75 and 71 million years ago, during the Late Cretaceous epoch.
facts.quote: This geological formation is estimated to date back to the Campanian stage (between 75 million and 71 million years ago) of the Late Cretaceous epoch.

facts.statement: The Djadochta Formation was deposited by wind processes in an arid environment with sand dunes and intermittent streams under a semi-arid climate.
facts.quote: The abundant sediments—sands, sandstones, or caliche—of the Djadochta Formation were deposited by eolian (wind) processes in arid settings with fields of sand dunes and only intermittent streams, as indicated by very sparse fluvial (river-deposited) sedimentation, under a semi-arid climate.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Velociraptor mongoliensis was found at the Flaming Cliffs, while the "Fighting Dinosaurs" were found at the Tugrik Shire locality.
facts.quote: The type specimen was discovered at the Flaming Cliffs site (sublocality of the larger Bayn Dzak locality/region), while the "Fighting Dinosaurs" were found at the Tugrik Shire locality (also known as Tugrugeen Shireh and many other spellings).

facts.statement: A Velociraptor skeleton found in Utah was five-and-a-half-feet tall, which was larger than the species depicted in the Jurassic Park films.
facts.quote: Later, after we had designed and built the raptor, there was a discovery of a raptor skeleton in Utah, which they labeled 'super-slasher.' They had uncovered the largest Velociraptor to date and it measured five-and-a-half-feet tall, just like ours.

facts.statement: The male Velociraptor in Jurassic Park III had quill-like structures on its head and neck that did not resemble the actual feathers of the animal.
facts.quote: For Jurassic Park III, the male Velociraptor was given quill-like structures along the back of the head and neck, but these structures do not resemble the feathers that Velociraptor would have had in reality due to reasons of continuity.

facts.statement: Velociraptor is a genus of two known dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaurs that lived between 75 and 71 million years ago during the Campanian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Velociraptor (lat. 'ladrón veloz') es un género con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios terópodos dromeosáuridos que vivieron hacia finales del período Cretácico, hace de 75 a 71 millones de años, durante el Campaniaense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey, much smaller than the two-meter-tall, ninety-kilogram dinosaurs shown in novels and films.
facts.quote: El Velociraptor era aproximadamente del tamaño de un pavo, considerablemente más pequeño que los dinosaurios de dos metros de altura y noventa kilogramos que aparecen en novelas y películas, más similares a Deinonychus.

facts.statement: A famous fossil specimen shows a Velociraptor engaged in a battle with a Protoceratops.
facts.quote: Un espécimen particularmente famoso es el que muestra a un Velociraptor enzarzado en una batalla con un Protoceratops.

facts.statement: The size range of Velociraptor varies from 1.5 to 2.07 meters in length, with a body mass between 15 and 18.3 kilograms.
facts.quote: El rango de tamaños varía de 1.5 a 2.07 m de largo, con una masa corporal de entre 15 y 18.3 kg.

facts.statement: Velociraptor may have been covered in feathers, including complex feathers on its forearms similar to the flight feathers of modern birds.
facts.quote: Es posible que Velociraptor estuviese cubierto de plumas, no solo plumón cobertor sino que también presentara plumas complejas en los antebrazos semejantes a las rémiges de las aves actuales.

facts.statement: The genus Velociraptor was named by Osborn in 1924.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osborn, 1924

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Velociraptor is Velociraptor mongoliensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Velociraptor mongoliensis

facts.statement: A second species, Velociraptor osmolskae, was described by Godefroit et al. in 2008.
facts.quote: subdivision: Velociraptor osmolskae Godefroit et al., 2008

facts.statement: Synonyms for Velociraptor include Ovoraptor (Osborn, 1924), Veiociraptor (Barsbold, 1983), and Velociraptoe (Dong, 1977).
facts.quote: synonyms: Ovoraptor Osborn, 1924 Veiociraptor Barsbold, 1983 Velociraptoe Dong, 1977

facts.statement: Fossils of Velociraptor mongoliensis have been found in Central Asia in Mongolia, while a second species, Velociraptor osmolskae, was named in 2008 from cranial material found in Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Durante mucho tiempo solo se ha reconocido una especie, Velociraptor mongoliensis, cuyos fósiles se han hallado en Asia Central, en Mongolia, pero una segunda especie, Velociraptor osmolskae, fue nombrada en 2008 a partir de material craneal procedente de Mongolia Interior, en China.

facts.statement: At least a dozen Velociraptor skeletons have been unearthed, which is the largest number discovered for any dromaeosaurid.
facts.quote: con no menos de una docena de esqueletos fósiles desenterrados, la mayor cantidad descubierta de un dromeosáurido.

facts.statement: The premaxilla was the most anterior bone of the skull and was longer than it was tall.
facts.quote: El premaxilar era el hueso más anterior del cráneo y era más largo que alto.

facts.statement: The maxilla was almost triangular in shape and was the largest element of the snout.
facts.quote: El maxilar tenía forma casi triangular y era el elemento más grande del hocico.

facts.statement: The premaxilla had four tooth sockets for four teeth, while the maxilla had eleven sockets for eleven teeth.
facts.quote: El premaxilar tenía cuatro alvéolos, lo que significa que se desarrollaron cuatro dientes, y el maxilar tenía once alvéolos.

facts.statement: The dentary bone contained between fourteen and fifteen tooth sockets.
facts.quote: En el dentario, estaban presentes entre catorce y quince alvéolos.

facts.statement: Velociraptor's teeth were mostly homodont (similar in shape) and had serrations that were more pronounced on the back edge than the front.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Velociraptor eran bastante homodontos, iguales en forma, y tenían varios dentículos, cada uno más aserrado en el borde posterior que en el frontal.

facts.statement: The upper jaw teeth were thinner and curved backward, with the lower edge significantly more serrated than the upper, possibly an adaptation to capture and hold fast-moving prey.
facts.quote: Los dientes maxilares eran más delgados, recurvados y, sobre todo, el extremo inferior estaba considerablemente más aserrado que el superior, posiblemente una adaptación que mejoró su habilidad para capturar y retener presas veloces.

facts.statement: The second finger was the longest of the three, while the first finger was the shortest.
facts.quote: El segundo dígito fue el más largo de los tres dígitos presentes, mientras que el primero fue el más corto.

facts.statement: The wrist bone structure prevented the wrist from pronating, forcing the palm to face inward rather than downward.
facts.quote: La estructura de los huesos del carpo, la muñeca, impidió la pronación de la muñeca y obligó a sujetar la superficie de la palma hacia adentro, medialmente, no hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Velociraptor's tail was rigid, featuring long bony projections called zygapophyses on top of each vertebra and ossified tendons underneath.
facts.quote: La cola de Velociraptor era rígida, con largas proyecciones óseas, zigoapófisis, en la parte superior de cada vértebra y con tendones osificados bajo ella.

facts.statement: The rigidity allowed the tail to act as a single bar-like unit, preventing vertical movement between vertebrae.
facts.quote: La rigidez reforzaba toda la cola permitiendo que actuara como una unidad con forma de barra, previniendo movimientos verticales entre las vértebras.

facts.statement: At least one specimen preserves a series of intact tail vertebrae in an 'S' curve, suggesting considerable horizontal flexibility.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, por lo menos un espécimen preserva una serie de vértebras caudales intactas en una curva con forma de 'S', sugiriendo que hubo una considerable flexibilidad horizontal.

facts.statement: These tail adaptations likely provided balance and stability when turning, especially at high speeds.
facts.quote: Estas adaptaciones de la cola probablemente aportan equilibrio y estabilidad al girar, especialmente a altas velocidades.

facts.statement: In 2010, Hone et al. published findings from 2008 regarding isolated teeth considered to be from Velociraptor alongside bite marks on a Protoceratops bone in the Bayan Mandahu Formation.
facts.quote: En 2010 Hone et al. publicaron un artículo sobre su descubrimiento de 2008 de dientes aislados que consideraron de Velociraptor junto a unas marcas de mordida en el hueso de un supuesto Protoceratops en la formación Bayan Mandahu.

facts.statement: The authors concluded the finding represented the final stage of carcass consumption by Velociraptor, after the predator had eaten other parts of a recently dead Protoceratops before biting the jaw area.
facts.quote: Los autores concluyeron que el hallazgo representaba «la última etapa de consumo del cadáver por parte del Velociraptor», ya cuando el depredador se había comido otras partes de un Protoceratops recién muerto, antes de morder en el área de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: In 2012, Hone and colleagues published an article describing a Velociraptor specimen with a long bone from an azhdarchid pterosaur in its throat.
facts.quote: En 2012 Hone y colaboradores publicaron un artículo que describía un espécimen de Velociraptor con un hueso largo de un pterosaurio azdárquido en su garganta.

facts.statement: This finding was interpreted as evidence of scavenging behavior.
facts.quote: Este hallazgo fue interpretado como una prueba de comportamiento carroñero.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests Velociraptor was an opportunistic and active predator that also scavenged during droughts, famines, illness, or depending on the animal's age.
facts.quote: La evidencia fósil sugiere que Velociraptor comiendo carroña también indica que era un animal oportunista y activamente depredador, que se alimentaba de carroña en tiempos de sequía o hambruna, si tenía problemas de salud o según la edad del animal.

facts.statement: A 2021 phylogenetic analysis by James G. Napoli and his team during the description of Kuru showed the position of Velociraptor within Eudromaeosauria.
